title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: LENNY AND THE CAT
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Lenny Szabo, a retired ice cream truck driver from Erie, Pennsylvania.
He lived alone, and told everyone he liked it that way. Then a cat moved onto his porch.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE INTRUDER
segments.quote: We can judge the heart of a man by his treatment of animals.
segments.author: Immanuel Kant
lines: One cold November morning, a skinny orange cat sat on his mat like he paid rent.
Lenny waved a broom. Shoo.
Across the street, his neighbor Mrs. Okafor called out a line from the philosopher Immanuel Kant:
We can judge the heart of a man by his treatment of animals.
Lenny grumbled, and put out a can of tuna. Just so nobody judged his heart.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE COOLER
segments.quote: I learned that it is the weak who are cruel, and that gentleness is to be expected only from the strong.
segments.author: Leo Rosten
lines: The cat ate the tuna, then hissed at him like he owed it money.
Lenny named him Sarge. When the first snow came, Lenny remembered the writer Leo Rosten:
I learned that it is the weak who are cruel, and that gentleness is to be expected only from the strong.
So he turned his old ice cream cooler into a cat house, lined with his second-best sweater.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: TAMED
segments.quote: You become responsible, forever, for what you have tamed.
segments.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
lines: Every day, Lenny sat one step closer. By Christmas, Sarge slept on his lap.
His granddaughter Mia read him a line from The Little Prince, by Antoine de Saint-Exupéry:
You become responsible, forever, for what you have tamed.
Lenny bought a real cat bed, and booked the vet for Monday.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BLIZZARD
segments.author: Aristotle
lines: Sunday night, a lake-effect blizzard buried Erie. In the morning, Sarge was gone.
Lenny searched for two days. On day three, Mrs. Okafor brought cocoa and a line from Aristotle:
Hope is a waking dream.
So Lenny kept dreaming with his boots on, knocking on every door. He met more neighbors that day than in ten years.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE SURPRISE
segments.quote: It's no use going back to yesterday, because I was a different person then.
segments.author: Lewis Carroll
lines: At the last house, a young welder named Danny opened his garage.
There was Sarge, in a laundry basket, with five tiny kittens. Sarge was a mom.
Lenny laughed so hard he sat in the snow. He thought of Lewis Carroll's Alice:
It's no use going back to yesterday, because I was a different person then.
The grumpy man with the broom was gone. He carried the whole family home.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE JINGLE
segments.quote: Disinterested love for all living creatures, the most noble attribute of man.
segments.author: Charles Darwin
lines: In May, Lenny played his truck's jingle one more time. Free ice cream. Kittens to meet.
On the side, he painted a line from Charles Darwin:
Disinterested love for all living creatures, the most noble attribute of man.
Love that wants nothing back. Every kitten found a home on that street. Sarge kept the porch.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Be kind. Be gentle. Take care. Keep hoping. Let yourself change. Love freely.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Be kind. Be gentle. Take care of what you tame. Keep hoping. Change. Love freely.
My own cat ignores me completely. I think we're very happy.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
